Done. `src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__widen_idempotency_key.sql` widens `payment.idempotency_key` from `VARCHAR(64)` to `VARCHAR(128)`; `NOT NULL` is preserved by that form.

What I checked and found:

- **`V1__init.sql:3`** — the one and only place the key length is constrained. I left V1 untouched rather than editing `64` → `128` in place: a versioned migration that's already been applied to any database won't re-run, and editing it would break Flyway's checksum. A fresh database now runs V1 then V2 and lands at 128.
- **`Payment.java:14`** — `@Column(nullable = false)` sets no `length`, so JPA is not constraining it (Hibernate's implicit default is 255, already wider than the column). Nothing to widen.
- **`PaymentValidator.check`** — only null/blank checks, no length cap.
- **`payment.graphqls:12`** — plain `String!`, no length directive.
- Controller, DTO, repository, and the legacy calculator never touch key length.

Two things to confirm on your side:

- **SQL dialect.** There's no JDBC driver or `application.properties` in the repo, so I couldn't tell which database this targets. I used `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE`, the standard-SQL spelling that PostgreSQL and H2 both accept. On MySQL/MariaDB it needs to be `MODIFY idempotency_key VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL` instead.
- **Migration runner.** Flyway isn't a dependency in `pom.xml`, so whatever applies `V1` today (test fixture, external tooling) also needs to pick up `V2`.

I didn't run a build — the change is SQL only, and the single existing test (`PaymentServiceTest`) doesn't touch the schema.
